chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Misma' ibn Abd al-Malik, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The adulterer is whipped more intensely than the drinker of wine, and the drinker of wine is whipped more intensely than the slanderer, and the slanderer is whipped more intensely than the one who receives ta'zir (disciplinary punishment).'

key_terms.الْقَاذِفُ: The slanderer (one who accuses others of unchastity)

ai.seo_question: What is the hierarchy of punishment severity between adultery, wine drinking, and slander in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes a hierarchical severity among the major hadd punishments, positioning zina as the most severe, followed by shurb al-khamr, and then qadhf. This ranking reflects the jurisprudential weight placed on the violation of lineage and social honor, with the adulterer receiving the harshest physical penalty. The narration underscores the Prophet's authority in defining the relative gravity of these offenses within the Shia legal tradition.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman, from Misma’a Bin Abdul Mallik, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The adulterer would be whipped more intensely than the drinker of the wine, and the drinker of the wine would be whipped more intensely than the slanderer, and the slanderer would be whipped more intensely than the rebuker (of a sinner)’.
